# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)</sub>
- **Status:** widow  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058)</sub>
- **Role:** housekeeper and housemother for college students at Patty's Place  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)</sub>
- **Titles:** Aunt Jamesina  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c19 P41](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0041)</sub>; Aunty  <sub>[v3 c35 P0](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0000), [v3 c35 P2](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0002)</sub>

## Appearance

She is a tiny old woman with a softly-triangular face, pink cheeks, and snow-white hair worn in quaint little puffs over her ears. Her large, soft blue eyes shine with unquenchable youth and hope.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)_

## Personality

Aunt Jamesina possesses a cheerful, indulgent, and youthful disposition. She is open about being old-fashioned in her style and opinions, preferring comfort over formality. Charming and patient, she acts as a forgiving housemother who lets the young women make their own choices while maintaining her own dry humor. She candidly owns up to her own past flaws and likes to joke about her former and current suitors.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005), [v3 c35 P15](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0015), [v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021), [v3 c35 P23](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0023)_

## Goals

- Keep house for Stella, Anne, Priscilla, and Philippa at Kingsport  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>

## History

After her only daughter married and left for missionary work, Aunt Jamesina was left alone in a large house. At the suggestion of her niece Stella Maynard, she agreed to move to Kingsport to act as housemother for Stella, Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon at Patty's Place. She brought along her cat, the Sarah-cat, as well as Joseph, a colorful cat entrusted to her by a friend moving to Vancouver. Upon moving into Patty's Place, she quickly won the deep affection of the four students. During her time in Kingsport, she presided over the household with gentle humor, listened to the young women's romantic dilemmas, shared anecdotes of her own past suitors, and kept up correspondence with old widowers back home who held affection for her.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c16 P55](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0055), [v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058), [v3 c19 P25](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0025), [v3 c19 P33](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0033), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005), [v3 c35 P23](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0023), [v3 c35 P25](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0025)_

## Background by volume

- Named Jamesina after her father James, who drowned at sea a month prior to her birth  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- Her late husband used to call her cat the Sarah-cat  <sub>[v3 c16 P59](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0059)</sub>
- Her only daughter recently married and departed for the foreign mission field  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- Had numerous former suitors, including Jim Elwood, Dan Winston, Milton Edwards, and Horatio Reeve  <sub>[v3 c35 P25](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0025)</sub>

## Quotes

> I’m old enough to indulge myself in the matter of shoes and opinions.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> You mustn’t marry anybody you don’t love, Phil, when all’s said and done  <sub>[v3 c19 P33](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0033)</sub>

> I’ve a notion that such prayers don’t rise very far.  <sub>[v3 c35 P15](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0015)</sub>

> Holding spite doesn’t seem worth while when you get along in years.  <sub>[v3 c35 P17](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0017)</sub>

> There are three old widowers at home who have been casting sheep’s eyes at me for some time.  <sub>[v3 c35 P23](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0023)</sub>
